title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: The End

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa II script, Matsumoto Stadium, Nagano, 28 April 2002: "we have an exciting card including the crowning of the first ever PURE Champion, that being the Junior Heavyweight category with The End facing the HIT facing Kensuke Suzahara", ending with owner Alexander Miyagawa presenting the belt — "The first ever PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion... THE END!!!!!"

lost.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, Sapporo, 16 June 2002 — the champion's title on the line in a tag match, the commentary stating the stipulation ("We shouldn't forget that his Jr Heavyweight title is on the line in this match!" / "Right! Whoever pins him wins the belt!!"), Charlie Loc and The H.I.T. finishing The End with the double powerbomb into a blue thunder facecrusher the commentary calls the Double Neurotica, The H.I.T. covering for the three, and ring announcer Hanza Kibagame with the belt in hand: "Winner…and NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION…THE HARDCORE ISOSCELES TRAPEZOID!!!"

how: Beat The H.I.T. and Kensuke Suzahara in a three-way, making The H.I.T. tap to Never Again, to become PURE's first ever champion.
note: PURE's own roster card for The End calls him "First ever PURE titleholder" and "First ever two-time PURE titleholder"; the second reign is a row of its own. The belt left him at Ikusa V on 16 June 2002, in a tag match his own title was put on, and he gave his own account of it backstage the same night — "I am baffled myself on the loss…but more baffled on how I lost the belt." The fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history carries the same change at its entry #2 and the same crowning at its entry #1, where it has him beat "The HIT and Kensuke Suzahara in a triple threat match to win the belt at Ikusa II" and then dates the reign "(4/14/02 - 4/28/02)" — a span that runs against its own sentence, since Ikusa II is the show of 28 April 2002 and 14 April 2002 is Ikusa. Both stand.

title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: The HIT

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, Sapporo, 16 June 2002 — the champion's title on the line in a tag match, the commentary stating the stipulation ("We shouldn't forget that his Jr Heavyweight title is on the line in this match!" / "Right! Whoever pins him wins the belt!!"), Charlie Loc and The H.I.T. finishing The End with the double powerbomb into a blue thunder facecrusher the commentary calls the Double Neurotica, The H.I.T. covering for the three, and ring announcer Hanza Kibagame with the belt in hand: "Winner…and NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION…THE HARDCORE ISOSCELES TRAPEZOID!!!" PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) numbers him its second champion, entry #2: "Pinned The End during a six man tag team match to win the title at Ikusa III". The bout the script carries is a six-man tag, and it is Ikusa V's; the fed's own two records name two different shows for the one change, and both stand.

lost.source: The record does not date the end of this reign. PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) gives the night and the manner at entry #3, where The End takes the belt back: "Pinned Inphino Blitz in a fatal four way match on Ikusa 6." No surviving PURE record holds or dates a show of that name. The change falls between 16 June 2002 and 28 July 2002, the night PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 bills The End as the defending PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion.

how: Pinned The End after the Double Neurotica, in a tag match the fed put the champion's own title on — whoever pinned The End won the belt.
note: The fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history numbers him its second champion and names the win, in a six man tag team match, at a show it calls Ikusa III; the script that carries that bout is Ikusa V's, of 16 June 2002, and both stand. The fed's own earlier paperwork bills The End because The End was champion when it was written — the division rankings of 2 May 2002 and the Ikusa IV card of 4 June 2002 both predate the change — and its own champions page carries only the holder of the moment, in states that begin in January 2003. His own PURE roster card is the one document that reads against the reign: its title-history field gives "None as of yet" and its award field is blank. The show's own script and its own ring announcer carry the change, and The End gave his own account of it backstage the same night — "I am baffled myself on the loss…but more baffled on how I lost the belt." All of it stands as written. The reign ended when The End took the belt back in a fatal four-way, on a show the fed's own history calls Ikusa 6 and no surviving record dates.

title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: Charlie Loc

won.source: PURE's own roster card for Charlie Loc bills him holder of the "PURE Jnr. Heavy Weight Title (Current)" and credits him as "First Man To Win a PURE Title Outside Of a PURE Ring"; the fed's own Axcess commentary says the same of him from the other side ("He won the Junior Heavyweight Title without even being on a PURE broadcast!"). The ring was PCW's. PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 script, 28 July 2002 — a two-fall match for both the PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship and the PCW Cruiserweight Title, The End defending both against Charlie Loc and Alexander Miyagawa under his own stipulation that "The PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship shall be determined by pinfall or submission, while the PCW Cruiserweight Championship will be decided by climbing the ladder". Charlie Loc takes the first fall — "MIYA'S HEAD HITS THE CHAIR, AND LOC HOLDS FOR THE PIN! 1! 2! 3!", called on air as "Charlie Loc has managed to win the PURE Junior Heavyweight Title" — and leaves with the belt: "Loc seems happy with his Junior Heavyweight Title as he holds it aloft as he departs the ring." PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) dates the same change at entry #4: "Pinned The End at PCW Wrestle Vessel in the first fall of a double Crusierweight title match to become PURE Juniorheavyweight champion. (7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)"

lost.source: PURE's own PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4 script, Ikusa Hall — "Jung Loc, going head to head with a bright young upstart in PURE, DJ Nygma, with Loc's PURE Jr. Heavyweight Title on the line", ending on a three count and the belt handed to the challenger; the fed's own Axcess replays the same match later. PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History") dates the reign "(7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)" and the change itself: "#5 - El Romantico — Pinned Jung Loc on Ikusa 4 under the guise of DJ Nygma to become the new PURE Juniorheavyweight champion (10/13/2002)". The fed's own news of 2 October 2002 still bills Ikusa 4 as ahead and its news of 4 October 2002 reports it "ready to go"; the show's own commentary places it after PCW's Red October of 6 October 2002.

how: Took the first fall of a two-fall match in PCW's ring, one that carried the PURE Junior Heavyweight and PCW Cruiserweight titles at once; lost the belt to a masked DJ Nygma on PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4.
note: PURE's own commentary names him "Jung 'Charlie' Loc" and bills him "Jung Loc" on air, the same man the fed's own roster card bills Charlie Loc. He arrives on PURE v2.0 Ikusa 1 in August 2002 billed "PURE's current Jr.Heavyweight champion", the belt over his shoulder; the commentary on v2.0 Ikusa 2 calls him "the former PURE Jr Heavyweight champion" while the shows either side of it bill him as the holder, and both readings stand. The two federations' own records of the win disagree on whom he pinned for the belt and both stand: PURE's own title history has him pin The End, and PCW's own script for the match has him pin Alexander Miyagawa while The End, defending both belts, was still in it. The win was taken in another federation's ring, and links that federation's own show.

title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: DJ Nygma

won.source: PURE's own PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4 script, Ikusa Hall — the challenger comes out of a Jr. Heavyweight battle royal earlier the same night, takes the belt on a three count, and the mask comes off: "DJ Nygma has just been revealed as none other than EL ROMANTICO!" The fed's own Axcess replays the match as "DJ Nygma vs. Jung Loc (c) - PURE JR.Weight Title Defense". PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History") dates it: "#5 - El Romantico — Pinned Jung Loc on Ikusa 4 under the guise of DJ Nygma to become the new PURE Juniorheavyweight champion (10/13/2002)", the same day it closes Charlie Loc's own reign. The fed's own news of 2 October 2002 still bills Ikusa 4 as ahead and its news of 4 October 2002 reports it "ready to go"; the show's own commentary places it after PCW's Red October of 6 October 2002.

lost.source: PURE's own Axcess: Jamar Wilson, holding the belt, says "the current PURE JR.Hevyweight champion is under PCW contract RIGHT NOW, in which I refer to El Romantico. That will be remedied when we crown a new champion here in PURE." The fed's own news row of 19 January 2003 then reports that "the PURE Jr.Weight title mini-tounry matches took place".

how: Won masked, as DJ Nygma, and unmasked in the ring the same night; the belt was decided again by tournament when PURE re-opened and its holder was under contract elsewhere.
note: PURE's own news row of 7 January 2003 calls him "the former PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion", quoting him by the El Romantico name. His own roster card's title-history line reads "none" in every layer of the deposit, against the fed's own champions page, which carries "Champion: El Romantico" in its January 2003 state, and against the Axcess script — recorded as a disagreement, not resolved. The reign is filed under the identity the unmasking revealed, with the masked billing on the label.

title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: Radiant

won.source: Radiant's own PURE roster card carries the reign as a dated defence ledger: "First reign as PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion - 1/26/03 to 00/00/00" and "1. (1/26/03 @ Hakatanomori Football Stadium) Radiant beat Isao Asai (30:15) by pinfall (Belt won)." PURE's own news row of 26 January 2003 reports the same night: "titles were decided", "a 5-star JR.Weight title match". PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) closes on him, entry #6: "Became champion upon restart of PURE in January 2003."

how: Beat Isao Asai in 30:15 by pinfall at Hakatanomori Football Stadium, in the tournament PURE ran for the belt when it re-opened.
note: No script for the 26 January 2003 show survives in the record, so this reign's own winning event carries its date from the fed's own roster card and links no page. Three defences follow, on Radiant's own card and on the shows themselves: Isao Asai at Tosu Stadium on 9 February 2003 (13:55, a Moonsault), Isao Asai at the Tokyo Dome on 2 March 2003 (11:42, a Shining Wizard), and El Mesias at Budokan Hall on 9 March 2003. The fed's two records of that last one disagree and both are kept: the card reads "(15:00) when the Time Limit experied", the show's own script has the referee stop it "due to a DOUBLE COUNT OUT! Therefore, this match is a draw!" with Radiant still champion.

title: pure-jr-heavyweight
label: The End

won.source: PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders), entry #3: "Pinned Inphino Blitz in a fatal four way match on Ikusa 6." No surviving PURE record holds or dates a show of that name. PURE's own roster card for The End bills him "Two-Time PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion" and "First ever two-time PURE titleholder", and he says it in his own words on PCW's own broadcast of 28 July 2002: "The PURE Junior Heavyeweight Title was the first title awarded and I won it twice!"

lost.source: PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 script, 28 July 2002 — a two-fall match for both the PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship and the PCW Cruiserweight Title, The End defending both against Charlie Loc and Alexander Miyagawa under his own stipulation that "The PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship shall be determined by pinfall or submission, while the PCW Cruiserweight Championship will be decided by climbing the ladder". Charlie Loc takes the first fall — "MIYA'S HEAD HITS THE CHAIR, AND LOC HOLDS FOR THE PIN! 1! 2! 3!", called on air as "Charlie Loc has managed to win the PURE Junior Heavyweight Title" — and leaves with the belt: "Loc seems happy with his Junior Heavyweight Title as he holds it aloft as he departs the ring." PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) dates the same change at entry #4: "Pinned The End at PCW Wrestle Vessel in the first fall of a double Crusierweight title match to become PURE Juniorheavyweight champion. (7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)"

how: Won it back in a fatal four-way, pinning Inphino Blitz on the show the fed's own title history calls Ikusa 6; lost it in PCW's ring at Wrestle Vessel 2002.
note: The second reign PURE's own roster card claims for him, placed by the fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history, which runs it as entry #3 between The H.I.T.'s reign and Charlie Loc's, and closed by PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002, where he defends the belt as champion and loses it. The night it began is named and so is the manner; the date is not recovered and is not guessed, and the record puts it between 16 June and 28 July 2002. No surviving record holds or dates a PURE show called Ikusa 6.

title: pure-world-heavyweight
label: Jesse Ramey

won.source: PURE's own Final Destinies script, Tokyo Dome, 2 March 2003 — the tournament final, with the belt presented to Ramey on his knees; his own roster card reads "First Ever PURE World Heavyweight Title (March 2nd, 2003-????)", and the fed's own champions page carries "Champion: Jesse Ramey" in its last state.

how: Won the four-man tournament PURE ran to crown its first World Heavyweight Champion, beating Eddie Mandrake in the final by pinfall.
note: The belt was announced in 2002 and stood vacant until this night: PURE's own news row of 18 February 2003 has the fed's vice president say "all the titles will be on this line, including the vacant PURE Heavyweight Championship". Defended at Budokan Hall on 9 March 2003 against Jason Marah, and the surviving record carries no later change. The fed billed the belt as both the PURE World Heavyweight Title (its champions page, its own title-history page, Ramey's roster card) and the PURE Heavyweight Championship (the Final Destinies and Budokan scripts) in the same weeks.

title: pure-tag-team
label: Inphino Blitz and Mang-A-Hero

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, 16 June 2002: "our boss, Alexander Miyagawa and Ebola III will be joining forces against the team of Inphino Blitz and Mang-a-Hero in a bout for the first awarding of the PURE Tag Team Titles", ending "Our winners and new PURE Tag Team Champions....INPHINO BLITZ AND MANG-A-HERO!"

end.source: PURE's own title-history page (newsdata board 78): "#2 - Titles retired. Retired belts upon the reopening of PURE." The fed's own show commentary says the same from the other side on the Tosu Stadium script: "We were the FIRST AND LAST PURE TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS!" / "That's only because Mina retired that spot for the Trinity!"

how: Beat Ebola III and Alexander Miyagawa, Mang-A-Hero pinning Miyagawa after the Dragon Drive Z, in the match booked for the first awarding of the belts.
note: The only reign the belts ever carried. The fed's own title-history page numbers it #1 and its own announcer calls the pair "new PURE Tag Team Champions", which reads as a title change but is not one: the match was billed on air as "a bout for the first awarding of the PURE Tag Team Titles" and "will determine the first PURE Tag Team Champions", so Ebola III and Alexander Miyagawa were challengers for a vacant belt, not holders of it.

title: pure-trinity-tag-team
label: Shaun Styles and the Sushi Crew

won.source: PURE's own title-history page (newsdata board 78): "#3 - Trinity Tag Team Championship declared. Sushi Crew / Shaun Styles become new champions over Black Dragons." The fed's own PURE World video package shows the same moment — "A picture of Shaun Styles beating the Black Dragons appears as he picks up one of the Trinity Tag Team Championships and holds it high." The belts were instated on Axcess and the pair are already billed champions in the Tosu Stadium script.

lost.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003: "Well, we have new Trinty Champions, in the form of the Suburban Ninja Clan!"

how: Beat the Black Dragons for the belts PURE declared on its re-opening.
note: No script survives for the night this reign began: the fed's own title-history page, its own video package and its own later scripts all carry the win, and nothing else does, so the winning event carries a month and links no page. The pair were billed as a team of three throughout — Ryu Sotosucki and Otoshi Mishimoto of the Sushi Crew with Shaun Styles as their third, in the Sushi Crew's own words "albeit with Shaun Styles as our partner".

title: pure-trinity-tag-team
label: Suburban Ninja Clan

won.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003 — Ninjas 20, 22 and 23 against "the PURE Trinity Tag Team Champions, they are Shaun Styles and the SUSHI Crew", ending on a choke hold and "we have new Trinty Champions, in the form of the Suburban Ninja Clan!" The fed's own champions page carries "Champions: Suburban Ninja Clan" in its last state.

how: Ninjas 20, 22 and 23 beat Shaun Styles and the Sushi Crew, Ninja 20 finishing Styles with a choke hold.
note: Eight days later the Clan issued an open challenge through PURE's own press office to any three-man team in the federations PURE shared a host with, offering to defend the belts on those feds' own shows: "The Clan will send ninjas to its challengers' shows and defend its Trinity Tag Team belts there." The surviving record carries no such defence.

title: pure-all-asia
label: Kohana

won.source: PURE's own Final Destinies script, Tokyo Dome, 2 March 2003 — Kohana beat Senji Yulav by submission with the Swift Kill; "The referee presents Kohana his newly won title".

lost.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003: "your winner, in 10 minutes and 39 seconds via pinfall...and NEW PURE ALL ASIA CHAMPION....TENZANNN RAIIIZOOOO!!!"

how: Beat Senji Yulav by submission with the Swift Kill.
note: Seven days, and the fed said so itself on the night it ended — its own reporter to the new champion: "congrats on winning the All Asia championship from Kohana right after he won it at Final Destinies".

title: pure-all-asia
label: Raizo Tenzan

won.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003 — a pinfall at 10 minutes 39 seconds over Kohana, in a match the fed booked to settle which of its two brands the belt would follow.

how: Beat Kohana by pinfall in 10:39, and took the belt out of the head referee's hands rather than be presented with it.
note: His own PURE roster card dates the win "March 16, 2003" against the show's own script, which stages it on 9 March 2003 at Budokan Hall; the script was posted on 14 March and marked "(Taped)". Both readings are kept.

title: pure-all-asia
label: "The Universal Outlaw" Senji Yulav

won.source: Senji Yuvlav's own PURE roster card bills him "All Asia Champion (current)" and "First Ever Pure All Asia Champion"; the fed's own scripts bill him champion from its January 2003 shows onward. No document in the record carries the win itself.

lost.source: PURE's own Final Destinies script, Tokyo Dome, 2 March 2003: "THE WINNER OF THIS MATCH....AND NEEEEW PURE ALL-ASIA CHAMPION....KOHANAAAA!!!"

how: The first holder of the belt, on the fed's own roster card; the record does not carry how or when he won it.
note: Billed "Senji Yulav" on every PURE show script and "Senji Yuvlav" on his own roster card — the same man, spelled two ways by his own federation, recorded rather than resolved.
